newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs sows 7.9 mln ha grains, 56 pct of plan.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs sows 7.9 mln ha grains, 56 pct of plan.

text.p: Kazakhstan sowed 7.9 million hectares to grain, 56 percent of the planned area, as of May 26, the government said on Wednesday.
Wheat was sown on 6.4 million hectares, roughly corresponding to last year's level, it said in a report.
Government officials in the Central Asian state do not make forecasts for the grain harvest until sowing is completed in early June.
Grain analysts forecast a net harvest around 14 million tonnes, provided the weather remains mild and farmers manage to sow at least 12 million heactares to grains.
Last year Kazakhstan was hit by severe drought and harvested a disappointing gross 13.2 million tonnes of grain, or a net 11.6 million.
Experts and officials agree this year's weather is more favourable, with enough moisture in the soil after heavy rainfall in the spring.

Sowing on Kazakhstan's vast steppes started around three weeks ago, and the government said that some regions, like Kyzyl Orda in the south and Pavlodar in the north, have so far sown 80-82 percent of planned areas.
But farmers face their usual problems -- lack of fuel and spares for the obsolete pool of combine harvesters.
The report said the government "has done a lot to provide farms with enough machinery, spare parts, oils and lubricants".
It said that most fuel and oil products had been delivered to farmers in return for grain from the next harvest.
"The farms hit by last year's drought received from the state reserves a total of 153,000 tonnes of seeds," the government said.
